text: As with any training program, all exercises and skills should be progressive in nature. The first time athletes perform a new drill, they will not be familiar with the movement. A significant amount of attention by the athletes will be required to perform the drill. Once the athletes have become familiar with the drill (familiarity will vary depending on the difficulty of the drill) they will know some key aspects of the movement, but attention will still be needed when performing the drill. When practiced extensively, the athletes will develop better knowledge of the movement and will be able to perform the drill with less conscious attention to the specific movement patterns.
